newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: Caribbean meeting looks to fight money-laundering.
newsitem.headline: Caribbean meeting looks to fight money-laundering.

text.p: Scores of international bankers and financial officials will meet in the Cayman Islands beginning Wednesday to discuss ways to combat money-laundering, commercial fraud and other financial crimes.
"Perpetrators of unethical business practices are always changing their approaches and doing something new," Cayman Islands Finance Minister George McCarthy said in a statement Monday.
"The Cayman Islands have to continue to send a unified message from all sectors of the industry that it will not provide criminally minded individuals with a haven for the proceeds of their crimes."

Certain Caribbean countries have a reputation as centres for laundering money from drug trafficking and other illicit activities. More than 560 financial institutions are registered in the Cayman Islands, a British territory, with assets in excess of $480 billion.
About 140 delegates from the United States, Canada, the Bank of England, the British Channel Islands, and other Caribbean countries will attend the meeting.
